content.value_statement: Metabolomics researchers need reliable access to public study, compound, and RefMet data. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused Metabolomics Workbench REST API searches.
actual_capabilities: Retrieves public compound metadata by registry number, PubChem CID, KEGG ID, HMDB ID, formula, or InChI Key.
Finds study summaries, factors, analysis metadata, measured metabolites, and experimental data from public study IDs.
Standardizes metabolite names with RefMet and explores RefMet hierarchy by class, formula, mass, or identifier.
Searches mass spectrometry m/z values with selected databases, adducts, and mass tolerances.
Filters studies by analysis type, polarity, chromatography, species, sample source, disease, KEGG ID, or RefMet name.
Queries gene and protein records linked to metabolomics data, including symbols, IDs, sequences, and annotations.
limitations: It depends on the public Metabolomics Workbench API being available and stable.
It does not authenticate to private studies or restricted datasets.
It does not perform statistical validation or confirm biological causality.
Large result sets may need caching, delays, and manual review of returned fields.

use_cases.title: Find Studies for a Metabolite
use_cases.description: Locate public studies that measured a metabolite, then review metadata and available experimental data.

use_cases.title: Normalize Compound Names
use_cases.description: Convert common metabolite names into RefMet terms and compare identifiers across compound databases.

use_cases.title: Screen m/z Candidates
use_cases.description: Search m/z values with adduct and tolerance settings to generate candidate compound matches.

prompt_templates.title: Find Public Studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the metabolomics-workbench-database skill to find public studies measuring glucose. Return study IDs, titles, species, sample sources, and available data types.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Names
prompt_templates.prompt: Standardize these metabolite names with RefMet: citrate, glucose, and tyrosine. Include matched names, identifiers, and classification levels when available.

prompt_templates.title: Search m/z Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Metabolomics Workbench for m/z 180.0634 using M+H and 0.01 Da tolerance. Summarize candidate compounds and useful follow-up endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Build Study Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow for finding LC-MS human blood diabetes studies, standardizing key metabolites with RefMet, and retrieving study summaries and data endpoints.

output_examples.output: A concise table of matching study IDs, titles, organisms, sample sources, diseases, and links to summary or data endpoints.

output_examples.input: Standardize citrate and explain its RefMet context.
output_examples.output: The matched RefMet name, available identifiers, structural classification, and notes about name ambiguity or missing fields.

output_examples.input: Screen m/z 635.52 with a positive proton adduct.
output_examples.output: A ranked candidate list with database source, compound name, mass match context, and suggested compound detail lookups.

best_practices: Start with RefMet name standardization before searching studies by metabolite.
Record study IDs, endpoint paths, adducts, and tolerance settings for reproducibility.
Cache large reference responses and use reasonable delays for repeated public API calls.
anti_patterns: Treating m/z candidates as confirmed compound identities without orthogonal evidence.
Mixing common names and standardized names without documenting the mapping step.
Repeating broad API requests in loops without caching or rate control.

faq.question: What database does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the public NIH Metabolomics Workbench REST API and its RefMet nomenclature resources.

faq.question: Can it access private studies?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes public REST endpoints and does not provide authentication for restricted datasets.

faq.question: Does it identify unknown compounds automatically?
faq.answer: No. It returns candidate matches from m/z searches. Scientific confirmation needs additional evidence.

faq.question: Can it download complete study data?
faq.answer: Yes, when the public API exposes the study data endpoint for the selected study ID.

faq.question: Which formats are supported?
faq.answer: The referenced API examples focus on JSON and tab-delimited text responses.

faq.question: Is this useful in Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides endpoint guidance that Claude Code, Codex, or Claude can use for research workflows.
